examples.en: My friend is holding a solo exhibition next month.
I went to the painter's first solo exhibition.

examples.ko: 개인전에서는 한 사람의 작품만 볼 수 있어요.
examples.en: At a solo show you can see only one person's works.
He won the gold medal in the individual table tennis event.
This tournament is split into team and individual events.

examples.ko: 개인전 준비로 요즘 잠을 거의 못 자요.
examples.en: I hardly sleep these days preparing for my solo show.

explain: 개인전은 두 가지로 써요. 미술에서는 한 작가의 작품만 모은 전시회이고, 운동에서는 팀이 아닌 한 사람이 겨루는 경기예요. 반대말은 전시회에서는 여럿이 함께 여는 '단체전', 경기에서도 '단체전'이에요.

phrases.en: That painter is holding a solo exhibition in Seoul.
phrases.nuance_ko: 작가가 혼자 전시회를 할 때 가장 흔하게 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common phrase for an artist holding a solo show.

phrases.en: This match is a team event, not an individual one.
phrases.nuance_ko: 개인전의 반대말로, 여럿이 함께 하는 전시나 경기예요.
phrases.nuance_en: The opposite of 개인전: a show or match done by a group.

phrases.en: My younger sibling competed in the individual swimming event.
phrases.nuance_ko: 운동 이름을 앞에 붙여 혼자 겨루는 경기를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Put a sport name before it to mean an individual event.

explain_en: Gaeinjeon has two uses: in art it is an exhibition of one artist's work, and in sports it is a match where one person competes rather than a team. The opposite in both cases is 단체전, a group show or team event.

examples.en: The city holds a festival every year.
Do you know the country that hosted the Olympics?
The school will hold a sports day in autumn.
There's a lot to prepare to host a competition.
After holding the exhibition, it became very popular.
We held a small concert.

explain: 축제, 대회, 전시회 같은 큰 행사를 여는 주최자가 쓰는 말이에요. 작은 모임이나 파티에는 '열다'나 '하다'가 자연스러워요. 열리는 행사를 주어로 하면 '개최되다'를 써요.

phrases.en: The school hosts a singing contest.
phrases.nuance_ko: '대회, 축제, 전시회'처럼 큰 행사와 잘 어울려요.
phrases.nuance_en: Pairs well with big events like contests, festivals, and exhibitions.

phrases.example: 시는 다음 달에 전시회를 개최할 예정이에요.
phrases.en: The city plans to hold an exhibition next month.
phrases.nuance_ko: 앞으로 열 계획이 있을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when an event is planned for the future.

phrases.en: Our neighborhood opens a small market.
phrases.nuance_en: For small events or gatherings, 열다 sounds more natural.

explain_en: Used by an organizer for big events such as festivals, contests and exhibitions. For small gatherings and parties, the plain verbs for 'open' or 'do' sound natural. When the event is the subject, the passive form is used.

dis.h: hold an event at a time or place

p.n: 주최하다 says you are the official organizer, not just that it is held.

examples.en: In college, I set off on a no-money trip with a friend.

examples.ko: 요즘은 무전여행을 하는 사람이 많지 않아요.
examples.en: These days not many people travel without money.

examples.ko: 무전여행 중에 낯선 아주머니가 밥을 주셨어요.
examples.en: During the trip, a stranger woman gave me a meal.
I heard my father even went on no-money trips when he was young.

examples.ko: 돈 없이 가는 무전여행은 위험할 수 있어요.
examples.en: A trip with no money can be dangerous.
A trip with no money? That's really brave of you.

explain: 돈을 거의 안 가지고 다른 사람의 도움으로 먹고 자며 다니는 여행이에요. 돈을 쓰되 싸게 다니는 '배낭여행'과는 달라요. 요즘은 위험해서 드물고, 옛날이야기나 추억담에서 자주 나와요.

phrases.en: I want to go on a no-money trip with a friend during vacation.
phrases.nuance_ko: '하다'와 함께 써서 그런 여행을 한다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: With '하다' it means doing that kind of trip.

phrases.en: I heard my father went on a no-money trip when he was young.
phrases.nuance_ko: '가다'와 함께 써서 그런 여행을 떠난다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: With '가다' it means setting out on that kind of trip.
phrases.en_equiv: to go on a no-money trip

phrases.en: The memories of the no-money trip are still vivid.
phrases.nuance_ko: 옛날 여행을 떠올리는 이야기에서 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used when recalling a trip from the past.

explain_en: It means travelling with almost no money, relying on others' help for food and a place to sleep. It differs from '배낭여행' (backpacking), where you still spend money but cheaply. It is rare today because of the risks and mostly comes up in old stories and memories.

examples.ko: 우리 팀은 겨울마다 제주도로 전지훈련을 가요.
examples.en: Our team goes to Jeju Island for a training camp every winter.

examples.ko: 야구 선수들이 따뜻한 곳에서 전지훈련을 해요.
examples.en: The baseball players do their camp training in a warm place.

examples.ko: 전지훈련 중에는 휴대폰을 마음대로 쓸 수 없어요.
examples.en: During the training camp, you can't use your phone freely.
This training camp takes place abroad for two weeks.

examples.ko: 전지훈련에서 돌아온 선수들이 많이 힘들어 보여요.
examples.en: The players back from the training camp look very tired.

examples.ko: 동생은 축구부 전지훈련에 참가하려고 돈을 모았어요.
examples.en: My younger brother saved money to join the soccer club's training camp.

explain: 스포츠 팀이 평소 훈련하는 곳을 떠나 다른 지역이나 외국에서 하는 훈련이에요. '합숙 훈련'은 함께 지낸다는 점이, 전지훈련은 장소를 옮겨 간다는 점이 중심이에요. 보통 '전지훈련을 가다/떠나다/하다'라고 말해요.

phrases.en: The baseball team leaves for out-of-town training tomorrow.
phrases.nuance_ko: 훈련하러 다른 곳으로 출발한다는 느낌이 강해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Stresses the idea of setting out for training somewhere else.

phrases.en: The soccer team is preparing for training abroad.
phrases.nuance_ko: 다른 나라로 가서 하는 훈련을 말할 때 앞에 '해외'를 붙여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Add 해외 in front when the training takes place in another country.

phrases.en: The players are in training camp in Jeju right now.
phrases.nuance_ko: 지금 훈련하고 있는 상태를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say the team is currently in the middle of the training.

explain_en: It is training a sports team does away from its usual base, in another region or abroad. '합숙 훈련' focuses on living together, whereas 전지훈련 focuses on moving to another place. People usually say '전지훈련을 가다/떠나다/하다'.

examples.ko: 체조 선수가 평행봉 위에서 멋진 동작을 보여 줬어요.
examples.en: The gymnast showed an amazing routine on the parallel bars.
He won the gold medal in the parallel bars event.
I hang on the parallel bars and work out every day.
There are parallel bars in the park, so it's good for exercising.

examples.ko: 평행봉을 잡을 때는 손이 미끄럽지 않게 해야 해요.
examples.en: When you grab the parallel bars, your hands must not be slippery.

examples.ko: 오늘 체육 시간에 평행봉을 처음 해 봤어요.
examples.en: Today in PE class I tried the parallel bars for the first time.

explain: 체조 종목이면서 그 기구 이름이에요. 철봉과는 다른 기구이고, 공원 운동 기구로도 자주 볼 수 있어서 체조 이야기와 운동 이야기 둘 다에 나와요.

phrases.example: 공원 평행봉을 잡고 몸을 들어 올렸어요.
phrases.en: I held the parallel bars in the park and lifted my body.
phrases.nuance_ko: 공원 운동 기구로 쓸 때 자주 하는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common phrase when using it as park exercise equipment.

phrases.en: Applause poured in when the parallel bars routine ended.
phrases.nuance_ko: 체조 경기에서 선수의 동작을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for a gymnast's routine in competition.

phrases.example: 평행봉 운동은 팔 힘을 기르는 데 좋아요.
phrases.en: Parallel bars exercises are good for building arm strength.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when talking about exercising with the equipment.

explain_en: It is both a gymnastics event and the name of the apparatus. It is a different piece of equipment from the '철봉' (horizontal bar), and since you also often see it as park exercise equipment, it comes up in both gymnastics and workout talk.

examples.en: We held my father's sixtieth birthday party at a restaurant.
This weekend I'm going to my eldest aunt's sixtieth birthday party.

examples.ko: 요즘은 환갑잔치 대신 가족 여행을 가는 집도 있어요.
examples.en: These days some families take a trip instead of holding a sixtieth birthday party.

examples.ko: 할머니 환갑잔치 때 온 가족이 모였어요.
examples.en: The whole family gathered for my grandmother's sixtieth birthday party.
At the party, the son sang a song for his parent.

examples.ko: 환갑잔치 준비 때문에 요즘 정신이 없어요.
examples.en: I've been swamped lately preparing for the sixtieth birthday party.

explain: '환갑'은 60번째 생일(한국식 나이로 61세)을 말하고, 좀 더 격식 있게는 '회갑'이라고 해요. 그 다음 큰 잔치는 '칠순잔치'예요. 어른께는 '환갑을 맞으시다'처럼 높여 말해요.

phrases.en: We held my parents' sixtieth birthday party at home.
phrases.nuance_ko: 잔치를 준비해서 치른다는 뜻으로, '하다'보다 조금 더 자연스러운 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means to host and organize the party; it sounds a bit more natural than just 'do' (하다).
phrases.en_equiv: to hold a sixtieth birthday party

phrases.en: I invited my relatives to the sixtieth birthday party.
phrases.nuance_ko: 잔치에 사람을 부를 때 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when inviting people to the party.
phrases.en_equiv: to invite to a sixtieth birthday party

phrases.en: The whole family gathered for my grandfather's sixtieth birthday party.
phrases.nuance_ko: '환갑잔치'와 뜻이 같지만 더 격식 있는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as 환갑잔치 but more formal.

explain_en: '환갑' is the 60th birthday (61 in Korean age), and a more formal word for it is '회갑'. The next big celebration is the '칠순잔치' (70th). For elders you say it respectfully, as in '환갑을 맞으시다'.
